title: Day 1: the machine, the frozen task and the baselines
text:
Machine: Intel i5-8250U, 4 cores / 8 threads, 7.6 GB RAM, no usable GPU (Intel UHD 620), so everything runs on the CPU. The task code (env.py, route_params.json and teacher.py, which env.py's route sensors use) is copied unchanged from the NEAT project and sha256-tested. 14 tests pass: determinism (same seed twice, reused and fresh env), boulder hit = crash, seed ranges, inputs come only from the observation history, numpy/torch network equivalence.

Baselines re-measured on 1,000 fresh flights (seeds 2,000,050,000+, fair boulder layout): pilot v1 72.2% [69.3-74.9], pilot v2 84.0% [81.6-86.1], the old 16-24-4 clone 84.6% [82.2-86.7]. The most common failure is coming to rest just outside the flags (6.6-6.9%), then crashes (4-5%), boulder hits (3.5%), timeouts (0.4-1.3%).

New warm start: a 2x128 network cloned from pilot v2 with DAgger (4 rounds, 789k steps, 97.7% action agreement) lands 83.5% vs the pilot's 85.9% on the same 1,000 analysis flights: the copy is as good as its source.

title: Bake-off, halfway: PPO from scratch is far ahead
text: Candidate A (PPO from a random 2x128 network, real task only) ran 45 minutes, 42 M steps. On its 200-flight real-task checks it reached 93-97% landed in the last minutes (off-pad 0%, timeouts 0-1%; almost all remaining failures are boulder hits, 2.5-6%). That is already well above every earlier agent (85%). Candidate B (PPO warm-started from the 83.5% clone) sits at 80-84% after 13 M steps: its low entropy (0.11) means it barely explores and stays close to the clone. Candidate C (evolution strategy) runs next. The single checks are best-of-many and flatter; the fair comparison is the 500 shared analysis flights at the end.

title: Bake-off result: PPO from scratch wins; main run M1 started
text:
Same 45 minutes of CPU each, then all three on the same 500 fresh analysis flights (real task):
A. PPO from a random 2x128 network: 91.4% [88.6-93.6]. Failures: boulder 6.6%, crash 1.2%, timeout 0.8%, off-pad 0%.
B. PPO warm-started from the 2x128 clone: 87.8% [84.6-90.4] (its start, the clone, flew 87.0% on the same flights: barely moved; it hardly explored, entropy 0.11).
C. Evolution strategy from the same clone: 83.4% [79.9-86.4], worse than its start after 124 generations.
Choice: PPO from scratch. It learns from every step, it isn't anchored to the pilot's habits (it never comes to rest off the pad, the pilot's main failure), and it was still improving: the average of its 200-flight checks went 90.8% (26 M steps) -> 93.8% (39 M). Its touchdowns are faster (median 0.25 vs 0.07 for the pilot) but they hold.
Where it fails: boulder hits, more often when the boulder floats 1-2.5 m off centre (10-12% failed) than near the middle (2-7%).
Main run M1 continues A's network and optimiser: stage 1 more real-task training, stage 2 hard cases (30% re-flown failed check seeds), stage 3 fine-tune (lr 1e-4). Supervised; checks every 10 iterations on 200 fresh flights.
